short: Ended the Anarchy, built the Angevin lands, and founded the English common law.
full:
Henry came to the throne in December 1154 under the settlement that ended nineteen years of civil war between Stephen and Henry's mother Matilda. He demolished unlicensed castles, recovered alienated royal estates, and inherited or married his way into an arc of territory running from Northumberland to the Pyrenees: England, Normandy, Anjou and, through Eleanor of Aquitaine, the south-west of France.

His lasting work was legal. The assizes of Clarendon and Northampton put royal justices on regular circuits, established jury presentment of criminals, and offered standard writs that pulled land disputes out of baronial courts and into the king's. This is the foundation of the English common law. His attempt to bring clerics under the same jurisdiction brought conflict with Thomas Becket, murdered in Canterbury Cathedral in 1170 by knights acting on the king's exasperation. Henry's last years were consumed by rebellions from his own sons, and he died at Chinon in 1189.
